battle.name: 第三次奴隸戰爭
battle.theater: 維蘇威火山至布拉提烏姆
battle.brief: 公元前73年拉提姆的角鬥士學校爆發逃亡，前73至前71年色雷斯奴隸斯巴達克斯在維蘇威火山起兵，擊敗大法官與執政官所部，最終戰死於布拉提烏姆。卡面的羅馬短劍是共和國軍團的制式冷兵器，也是義軍繳獲後迅速成建制裝備的關鍵軍械。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 公元前73年至前71年的第三次奴隸戰爭，發生在羅馬共和國本土的義大利中部與南部，性質上不是國家之間的戰爭，而是羅馬治下奴隸群體與羅馬國家機器之間的一場大規模內戰；沒有任何外國正式參與，也沒有形成跨國聯盟。起義方是拉丁姆與坎帕尼亞的奴隸，爆發點是卡普阿（Capua）附近、盧庫斯·班提亞圖斯（Lentulus Batiatus）名下的角鬥士學校；隊伍以色雷斯人斯巴達克斯為核心，另有高盧人、奇里西亞人、腓尼基人、希臘人與薩賓人陸續加入，坎帕尼亞的牧人（pastores）更在後段成建制地倒向義軍。羅馬方面的指揮系統由元老院統籌，軍事上分三級遞進：前73年先派大法官瓦里尼烏斯（Gaius Publius Varinius）率一支不大的追擊部隊進剿，瓦里尼烏斯陣亡後改由大法官倫圖盧斯（Publius Lentulus）接手，再到前72年由兩位執政官倫圖盧斯與格拉伯（Gaius Claudius Glaber）各率一個軍團作戰；前71年戰事升級，元老院指派執政官克拉蘇（Marcus Licinius Crassus）、執政官格利西亞（Gaius Claudius Glicia）與從西班牙回師的代執政官菲利普斯（Quintus Marcius Philippus）會師，另派大法官加西烏斯·卡西烏斯·隆吉努斯（Gaius Cassius Longinus）封鎖退路。羅軍的後勤以卡普阿等軍需城市為樞紐，軍械庫、工兵與攻城器具隨軍移動；各地殖民地與拉丁盟邦依例提供援軍與糧食。義大利的大莊園主是受直接衝擊的一方，莊園被焚、勞役人口流失，而羅馬的城鄉菁英在「鎮壓範圍」與「誰來出錢」之間分裂。整場戰役的地理範圍始終限定在義大利本土，沒有出現行省軍團參戰的記錄。
countriesEn: The Third Servile War of 73 to 71 BC was fought in central and southern Italy, inside the territory of the Roman Republic. In nature it was not a war between states but a large-scale civil war between enslaved populations and the Roman state machinery; no foreign power took part officially and no cross-border alliance was ever formed. The insurgents were enslaved people of Latium and Campania, and the outbreak began in the gladiatorial school of Lentulus Batiatus near Capua. The core of the band was the Thracian Spartacus, and Gauls, Cilicians, Phoenicians, Greeks and Sabines joined over time, while the herdsmen (pastores) of Campania later defected to the rebels in numbers. On the Roman side the whole affair was directed by the senate, and command escalated in three steps. In 73 BC the praetor Gaius Publius Varinius was sent out with a modest pursuit force; after Varinius was killed the praetor Publius Lentulus took over; in 72 BC the two consuls Lentulus and Gaius Claudius Glaber each led a legion. In 71 BC the war was upgraded: the consul Marcus Licinius Crassus was given overall charge and joined up with the consul Gaius Claudius Glicia and with Quintus Marcius Philippus, the propraetor returning from Spain, while the praetor Gaius Cassius Longinus was ordered to close the escape routes. Roman supply ran through the military depots of towns such as Capua, with armoury stores, engineers and siege equipment travelling with the columns; the colonies and the Latin allies supplied contingents and provisions as required. The great landowners of Italy were the party directly hit, their estates burned and their labour force dispersed, while the urban and rural elites of Rome split over how far the suppression should go and who should pay for it. The fighting itself never left Italian soil, and no provincial legions appear anywhere in the record of this war.
people: 核心人物是斯巴達克斯。他是色雷斯人，戰前被擄掠、販賣並在角鬥士學校受訓；據普魯塔克《斯巴達克斯傳》，他與七十餘名同伴自班提亞圖斯的學校脫逃，途中襲擊牧人取得長矛與炊具，登上維蘇威火山，隨後把零散逃奴、莊園逃工與復仇者編成隊伍，最後成為全軍的統帥。他沒有一支可以公開冊封的軍隊，也沒有羅馬式的指揮官結構，靠的是個人威信、對山林地形的熟悉，以及對羅馬正規戰術的逆向理解：避免正面與軍團對峙，專打分割、峽谷、夜襲與奪旗。起義初期的另一位關鍵人物是監工蓋烏斯·尼姆法埃斯（Gaius Nymphaeus），這是全戰役唯一留存的實物銘文，記載他在起義中喪命，也讓角鬥士學校究竟設在卡普阿郊區還是羅馬台塔切一帶成為學界聚論之地。羅馬方面先後登場的是：大法官瓦里尼烏斯（前73年，率軍追入拉提姆境內，兵敗陣亡）、大法官倫圖盧斯（前73至前72年，接手追剿）、執政官格拉伯與倫圖盧斯（前72年，兩個軍團，於薩拉魯斯河谷與「色雷斯山」兩役受挫）、執政官克拉蘇（前71年，主導戰局）。克拉蘇在此役中的形象最具戲劇性：普魯塔克記他在「活山」宿營巡視時，士卒因發現一隻狼而驚呼引他離營，其妻李西尼婭（Licinia）察覺近旁山坳中藏有敵軍，遂以帳幕與人數的假象使敵人誤以為營中兵馬充足而退走，克拉蘇因此免於一場潰滅。他的軍令亦嚴禁在無防禦處宿營、要求士卒自攜口糧以免輜重被襲、派騎兵巡邏警戒，顯示他對斯巴達克斯式游擊的修正。鎮壓階段另有兩個名字：克拉蘇之子普布利烏斯在前71年末的追擊戰中戰死；大法官隆吉努斯在坎帕尼亞南部追殲殘餘義軍，為最終收束出力。
peopleEn: The central figure is Spartacus. A Thracian, he had been captured, sold and trained in a gladiatorial school before the war; according to Plutarch's Life of Spartacus, he and some seventy companions broke out of Batiatus' school, cutting up the herdsmen they met on the road to take their spears and cooking utensils, then climbed Mount Vesuvius, and gradually assembled runaway slaves, escaped farm labourers and avengers into an army over which he came to command. He had no publicly acknowledged army and no Roman-style chain of command; what he had was personal authority, thorough knowledge of the mountains and an inverted grasp of Roman regular tactics — refusing to meet a legion in the open, and concentrating instead on separating the enemy, on defiles, on night attacks and on capturing standards. A second key person of the early phase is the overseer Gaius Nymphaeus, whose epitaph is the only material inscription preserved from the whole war; it records his death during the rising, and it keeps alive the scholarly debate over whether the gladiatorial school stood near Capua or on the Testace slope in Rome. On the Roman side the names appear in turn: the praetor Varinius, who pursued the rebels into Latium in 73 BC and was killed; the praetor Lentulus, who took over the suppression in 73 and 72 BC; the consuls Lentulus and Glaber, who with two legions lost at the valley of the Silarus and on the Thracian Mountain in 72 BC; and the consul Crassus, who directed the war in 71 BC. Crassus supplies the most dramatic figure in the campaign: Plutarch has him inspecting his camp on the Mons Vivarius, where the soldiers' alarm at a wolf drew him away from his tent, while his wife Licinia, having spotted enemy troops hidden in the neighbouring hollow, used the curtain walls and false numbers of her quarters to make the enemy believe the camp was fully manned, so that the enemy withdrew and the consul was spared a disaster. His orders are equally instructive: no camping without cover, soldiers to carry their own rations so the baggage trains could not be seized, and cavalry out on patrol; together they show how he corrected for the guerrilla style of Spartacus. Two more names belong to the closing phase: Publius Crassus, the consul's son, fell in the pursuit fighting at the end of 71 BC, and the praetor Longinus hunted down the remnants in southern Campania and closed the affair.
kits: 卡面這柄羅馬短劍（gladius），就是這場戰爭裡每一個羅馬士兵腰間的那把冷兵器。共和國晚期的短劍為雙刃、葉形尖，帶護手與柄頭，全長約六十至七十公分，劍身寬約五公分，重量接近一公斤，握柄纏皮或嵌木；它的用法不是揮砍，而是配合大盾（scutum）的弧面，貼身進盾後以短促的刺擊解決對手，並用盾緣磕擊、勾拉敵人兵刃。器物史講的那句話在第三次奴隸戰爭裡有兩層意思。其一，起義方是一群受過角鬥訓練的人，角鬥場上的武器選擇本就把刺擊放在第一位，角鬥士使用的正是這類短刃配小盾（parmula）的組合，技術素質是起義初期少數的優勢。其二，羅馬軍團每人配一柄短劍，作為標槍（pila）耗盡後的最後手段，也是在盾後應付短兵的最可靠兵器；義軍下山、掃掠莊園、打散羅軍支隊之後，繳獲的羅馬軍備裡最有價值的正是短劍、標槍、鎖子甲（lorica hamata）與大盾，這批制式裝備使起義軍在裝備水準上逼近正規部隊，也讓「盾加刺劍」的節奏第一次被成建制地用在一場沒有國家背景的內戰上。細節上，起義最初沒有短劍可用，普魯塔克說他們取的是牧羊人的長矛、鐵叉與廚刀，寬刃的廚刀正是短劍的雛形；義軍沒有冶煉與鍛造能力，補充兵器的唯一途徑是奪取敵軍與莊園的裝備。騎兵方面，斯巴達克斯在「色雷斯山」突圍時只帶出百餘騎，後擴為數百人，多為莊園繳獲的馬匹，無鎧或只有皮甲，靠速度與地形作戰。羅馬方面除短劍外還有投槍、長矛，騎兵配長柄刺槍（hasta）並以四馬一組編制作戰，工兵攜帶工具、帳幕、築城器材與野戰炊具，軍隊以野戰道路與渡口維持補給線。
kitsEn: The Roman short sword on the card, the gladius, is the cold weapon every Roman soldier in this war carried at his hip. The Republican gladius is double-edged with a leaf-shaped point, a guard and a pommel; it is roughly sixty to seventy centimetres long overall, the blade about five centimetres wide, and it weighs close to a kilogram, the grip wrapped in leather or fitted with wooden plates. It was not swung but thrust: the man worked behind the curve of the large shield (scutum), slipped inside the shield wall to deliver short, quick thrusts, and used the shield's rim to strike, to hook and to pull aside the enemy's weapon. That observation about the weapon has two layers of meaning here. First, the insurgents were men with gladiatorial training, and in the arena the choice of weapon already put the thrust first; the gladiator's pairing of a short blade with the small round shield (parmula) is exactly the combination these men knew, and their training was one of the few real advantages they had in the first weeks. Second, every man in a Roman legion carried a gladius as the last resort once the javelins (pila) were spent, and as the most reliable weapon in the shield wall once the fighting came to close quarters. After the rebels came down from the mountain, swept the estates and broke up Roman detachments, the most valuable things in the captured Roman kit were precisely the short swords, the javelins, the mail (lorica hamata) and the large shields; that standard equipment brought the insurgents up to a standard of equipment approaching a regular army, and it was the first time the rhythm of shield and gladius was drilled in formation in a civil war with no state behind it. In detail: at the beginning the rebels had no swords at all — Plutarch says they took the herdsmen's spears, iron forks and kitchen knives, and the broad kitchen knife is the ancestor of the gladius. The insurgents had no smelting or forging capacity, and the only way to replace weapons was to take them from enemies and estates. On the cavalry side, Spartacus broke out from the Thracian Mountain with a little over a hundred riders and later expanded this to several hundred, mostly horses seized from estates, without armour or in light leather, fighting on speed and terrain. On the Roman side, alongside the gladius, the kit included pila, the long spear, cavalry with the hasta and the four-horse troop system, and the engineers carried tools, tents, works of fortification and field cooking gear, while the army kept its supply line alive along the military roads and the river crossings.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術核心是不與軍團打正面。脫逃後七十餘人先上維蘇威火山，利用熔岩台地與林徑把追兵分隔，在山坳與狹窄道路上以劣勢兵力反覆襲擊；羅馬追擊部隊一旦展開縱隊進入峽谷，義軍便從側面高處以長矛與投石砸下，切斷隊形，再以少量人馬反覆切咬。瓦里尼烏斯曾分兵三路、封鎖通往坎帕尼亞的三條道路，義軍則以夜行避開封鎖、天亮前退回山中，把「封鎖」變成僵持。轉入坎帕尼亞後，義軍獲得大量自願加入的牧人與奇里西亞海盜，人數劇增，裝備雜亂，才開始承擔正面作戰的任務，於是必須建立較完整的戰鬥序列：步兵縱隊作前鋒與核心，兩翼以騎兵遮蔽，把敵軍分割成可以各個擊破的段落。最典型的是薩拉魯斯河谷一役，義軍以密集步兵方陣抵住羅軍騎兵衝擊，再以兩翼騎兵反擊，完成「以步制騎再反吃騎兵」的轉換。前72年的「色雷斯山」之役則相反，義軍在山中被格拉伯的部隊追上，斯巴達克斯以百餘騎殺穿重圍而走，七百名部眾戰亡，說明義軍一旦失去地形優勢就難以與正規軍抗衡。羅馬的戰術修正集中體現在克拉蘇身上：他禁止在無防禦處宿營，要求士卒自攜口糧以免輜重隊伍被襲，派騎兵巡邏警戒，並把作戰重點放在切斷義軍的營地與補給，而不是窮追；盧卡尼亞一役正是靠包抄奪取營壘、破壞糧秣與輜重，使斯巴達克斯的軍隊在損失慘重之後無法再靠搶奪補給維持。最終決戰則是義軍主動選擇的突圍戰，斯巴達克斯率少數人強行通過被封鎖的缺口，因準備不足而失敗；羅軍隨後以殘酷的展示手段收束戰局，把大批俘虜釘在從卡普阿通往羅馬的亞比亞大道兩側，讓補給線本身成為懲罰的場景。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the insurgents was to refuse a pitched battle with the legions. The seventy-odd men who had broken out first took to Mount Vesuvius, using the lava terraces and the forest paths to separate their pursuers, striking again and again out of the hollows and narrow defiles with inferior numbers; once a Roman column stretched out and entered a gully, the rebels brought it down from the higher ground to the side with spears and stones, cut the formation apart, and kept gnawing at it in small bands. Varinius once split his force three ways to seal the three roads leading to Campania, and the answer was to move by night, to let the sealing force freeze in place and to slip back into the mountains before dawn. Only after the insurgents entered Campania, where they were joined in numbers by volunteer herdsmen and by Cilician pirates, did their strength swell and their equipment become so mixed that they had to take on the tasks of a pitched battle; and then they needed a proper order of battle. Infantry columns formed the front and the core, cavalry covered the flanks, and the enemy was cut into segments that could be destroyed one at a time. The clearest example is the battle in the valley of the Silarus, where the rebels checked the Roman cavalry with a dense infantry front and then countered with the cavalry on both wings, turning a defence against horsemen into a defeat of the horsemen. The engagement on the Thracian Mountain in 72 BC went the other way: caught in the mountains, Spartacus cut through the encirclement with a little over a hundred riders and left, while about seven hundred of his men were killed, which showed that once the rebels lost the advantage of the ground they could not stand up to regular troops. The Roman correction of method is concentrated in Crassus: no camping without cover, soldiers carrying their own rations so the baggage trains could not be seized, cavalry sent out on patrol, and the emphasis shifted from pursuit to cutting the rebels off from their camp and their supply. The Lucanian battle turned on exactly that — the camp was taken by a flanking movement and the grain and baggage destroyed, so that after heavy loss Spartacus could no longer sustain the army by seizing what it needed. The last battle was a breakout chosen by the rebels themselves: Spartacus forced a way through a sealed gap with a handful of men and failed because he had not prepared. The Romans then closed the affair with a display of terror, nailing large numbers of prisoners along both sides of the Appian Way from Capua to Rome, so that the supply line itself became the place of punishment.
data: 數字多數來自普魯塔克與阿庇安，二人的記錄互相矛盾，只能當作量級參考。逃亡者：普魯塔克記為七十餘人，另有史料的說法從數十到數百不等。瓦里尼烏斯之役：羅軍陣亡約三百人（普魯塔克），義軍的損失以數十計。義軍總兵力：史料分歧最大，通行敘述有七萬、九萬乃至十二萬之說，可靠的下限只有數千人——阿庇安在描述最後一戰時提到斯巴達克斯率數千人突圍，即為當時確有數千精銳的佐證。羅軍兵力：前72年為兩個軍團；前71年克拉蘇集合六個軍團作戰，據普魯塔克其後把部隊增至十二個軍團。以共和國軍團約四千人（有學者按編制估算為四千八百）計，六個軍團約兩萬四千至兩萬九千人，十二個軍團接近五萬至六萬人；此為現代學者的推算，並非原文數字。損失：薩拉魯斯河谷一役羅軍陣亡約兩千人、被俘約八百人；「色雷斯山」一役義軍陣亡約七百人；盧卡尼亞一役克拉蘇損失約六千人。鎮壓規模：被釘在亞比亞大道上的俘虜，阿庇安記六千人，卡西烏斯·狄奧則記三千人，兩說並存；被公開販賣為奴者以萬計，阿庇安記約三萬人。距離與時間：維蘇威火山距卡普阿約三十公里，亞比亞大道自卡普阿至羅馬逾二百公里；整場戰爭自前73年秋天起至前71年秋收官，約兩年。月份：起義的確切月份不見於史籍，通行說法繫於前73年秋季，理由之一是采收季節莊園監管最為鬆散、逃奴最易隱入林地，此說屬推測而非定論。
dataEn: The figures come mostly from Plutarch and Appian, whose accounts contradict each other and can only be used as orders of magnitude. The escapees: Plutarch gives a little over seventy, while other sources range from a few score to several hundred. The affair with Varinius: about three hundred Romans killed (Plutarch), the rebel losses counted in tens. Total rebel strength: this is where the sources diverge most, with the common narrative giving seventy thousand, ninety thousand or even a hundred and twenty thousand men; the only reliable floor is a few thousand, and Appian's remark that Spartacus broke out at the last battle with several thousand men is evidence that there really were thousands of effectives. Roman strength: two legions in 72 BC; in 71 BC Crassus assembled six legions, and Plutarch has him raising the force to twelve. At about four thousand men to a Republican legion (some scholars compute four thousand eight hundred), six legions amount to some twenty-four to twenty-nine thousand men and twelve legions to something approaching fifty or sixty thousand; these are modern estimates, not figures from the sources. Losses: in the battle in the valley of the Silarus about two thousand Romans were killed and some eight hundred captured; on the Thracian Mountain about seven hundred of the rebels fell; in Lucania Crassus lost about six thousand men. The scale of the repression: of the prisoners nailed up along the Appian Way, Appian gives six thousand and Cassius Dio three thousand, and both figures stand; those sold publicly as slaves are counted in tens of thousands, Appian giving about thirty thousand. Distances and duration: Mount Vesuvius is about thirty kilometres from Capua, and the Appian Way from Capua to Rome runs beyond two hundred kilometres; the whole war ran from the autumn of 73 BC to the close of the autumn of 71 BC, roughly two years. Month: the exact month of the outbreak is not recorded in the sources; the usual dating places it in the autumn of 73 BC, one argument being that during the harvest season estate supervision was loosest and runaways easiest to hide in the woods — a conjecture rather than a certainty.
cause: 起義的直接契機是奴隸人口在義大利的膨脹與莊園制度的壓榨。公元前264年以來的三次馬其頓戰爭、前218至前201年的第二次布匿戰爭，以及前73年龐貝戰爭結束前的地中海征伐，把大批戰俘與被征服地區的居民販入義大利；土地兼併與戰俘買賣同時把這些人集中到拉丁姆與坎帕尼亞的大莊園、牧場、礦場與鹽田，形成人口稠密、監管嚴酷而申訴無門的勞動隊伍。角鬥士學校是其中最集中的爆發點：奴隸在學院中受高死亡率的對決訓練，脫逃無門，於是班提亞圖斯學校的一次逃亡成了導火索。結構性的原因還包括前兩次奴隸戰爭留下的記憶與未竟的整改：前134至前132年的西西里起義與前104至前100年的第二次奴隸戰爭都曾被元老院以「宣戰」處理，卻沒有解決莊園制度本身，阿庇安記載第二次動亂中元老院下令把義軍首領的家屬變賣為奴，鎮壓之後奴工迅速重新聚集。政治層面上，元老院對「是否派兵、由誰領兵」爭論不決，執政官任期即將屆滿的時候無人願意接手，拖延數月讓起義從數十人擴成數萬人的武裝；斯巴達克斯後來明確拒絕羅馬提出的「解散武裝、只保留一支部隊」的條件，等於宣布這不會是一場以讓步換取投降的談判。深層次則是法律與身份：奴隸在共和國的司法體系裡不是主體，沒有申訴、沒有財產、沒有離開主人的權利，任何一次莊園管事的克扣或毆打都可能直接變成集體逃亡。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of the rising was the swelling of the enslaved population in Italy and the pressure of the estate system. The three Macedonian wars since 264 BC, the Second Punic War of 218 to 201 BC and the Mediterranean campaigns that ended with the war against Pompey in 73 BC poured large numbers of prisoners and of inhabitants of conquered districts into Italy as chattel; and land consolidation and the trade in prisoners concentrated the same people on the great estates, ranches, mines and salt works of Latium and Campania, forming labour gangs that were dense, harshly supervised and without a means of appeal. The gladiatorial school was the most concentrated point of eruption: slaves there trained in bouts with a high rate of death and had no way out, so that a single escape from Batiatus' school became the fuse. Structural causes include the memory and the unfulfilled reforms of the two earlier servile wars: the Sicilian revolt of 134 to 132 BC and the second servile war of 104 to 100 BC were both handled by the senate as a declaration of war, and neither touched the estate system itself; Appian records that during the second disturbance the senate ordered the families of the rebel leaders sold into slavery, and the labour force reassembled quickly once the repression was over. At the political level the senate argued over whether to send troops and who should lead them; when the consuls' term was running out nobody wanted the command, and months of delay allowed a revolt of dozens to become an army of tens of thousands. Spartacus later refused outright the Roman terms — disband the arms but keep one band — which announced that this would not be a negotiation settled by concession. At the deepest level lie law and status: the slave was not a subject in the republican legal order, with no appeal, no property and no right to leave a master, and any single act of embezzlement or beating by an estate overseer could turn at once into a collective flight.
impact: 這場戰爭留下的不是戰場上的勝負，而是羅馬奴隸制度的一次被迫檢視。軍事上，義大利本土的步兵兵源在戰後更加吃緊，羅馬進一步倚重行省盟邦的援軍與外來雇傭兵，義大利社會的不安成為前1世紀政治動盪的一部分背景——雖然把第三次奴隸戰爭直接說成前91至前88年同盟戰爭的導火線，是學界仍有爭議的說法。法律上，元老院作出決議，凡在戰鬥中站在羅馬一方的獲自由人給予公民權，這讓大批參與者在鎮壓之後得到安置，也讓「為奴隸作戰」變成可以被容忍的立場；克拉蘇另向元老院提出把參戰者與降者的土地分給士兵的方案，最終未見落實。制度上，這場戰爭加速了義大利本土奴隸制的收縮與佃農關係的調整，莊園經營越來越依賴在義大利受雇的勞動力，而不再是集中於奴隸名下的集體耕作；常被說成「因這場戰爭而廢除角鬥比賽」的說法，其實過度簡化——鬥技比賽的廢止是前2世紀末至前1世紀初逐步完成的過程，與第三次奴隸戰爭的關聯有限。文化上，阿比亞大道兩旁的死者影像成為拉丁記憶裡「奴隸的命運」與「羅馬的秩序」兩種敘事共存的公共場景，斯巴達克斯則在十九、二十世紀的文學與影像中逐漸被改寫成「自由」的象徵。軍事史上，這場戰爭更被反覆用作「不正規戰爭如何對付正規軍」的案例：補給線被奪、夜間行軍、山地游擊與騎兵遮蔽，往往比正面會戰更決定戰局。
impactEn: What the war left behind was not a battlefield result but a forced examination of the Roman system of slavery. Militarily the supply of Italian infantry became tighter after the war, and Rome leaned further on reinforcements from the provinces, the allies and hired troops abroad; the unease of Italian society became part of the background to the political convulsion of the first century BC, though it remains a contested claim that this war directly caused the Social War of 91 to 88 BC. Legally the senate resolved that freedmen who had fought on the Roman side should receive citizenship, which gave many of those involved a settlement after the repression and made the position of fighting for slaves one that could be tolerated; Crassus separately proposed to the senate that land should be given to the soldiers who had served and to the defeated, and the proposal was never carried out. Structurally the war hastened the contraction of slavery in Italy itself and the adjustment of tenant relationships, as the running of the great estates came to depend more and more on wage labour hired in Italy rather than on collective work owned outright by masters; the claim that the gladiatorial games were abolished because of this war is in fact over-simplified, since the suppression of the games was a gradual process running from the late second to the early first century BC and had only a limited connection with the Third Servile War. Culturally the images of the dead along the Appian Way became a public place where two narratives — the fate of the enslaved and the order of Rome — coexisted in the Latin memory, while Spartacus was gradually rewritten in nineteenth- and twentieth-century literature and imagery into a symbol of freedom. In the history of military thought the war is used again and again to show how an irregular force fights a regular one: a captured supply line, movement by night, guerrilla fighting in the hills and the screening action of cavalry settled more battles than any pitched engagement.
result: 前71年，形勢終結於義軍主動選擇的突圍戰。斯巴達克斯在布拉提烏姆被克拉蘇、菲利普斯與格利西亞所部截住，率少數人強行突破時戰死，屍身未被尋回；其突圍部隊亦全數覆沒。殘餘勢力由大法官加西烏斯·卡西烏斯·隆吉努斯在坎帕尼亞南部追殲，克拉蘇之子普布利烏斯·克拉蘇在戰役中陣亡，鎮壓階段再失去一名主將。羅馬以展示與販賣兩種手段收束戰局：大批俘虜被釘在自卡普阿至羅馬的亞比亞大道上（阿庇安記六千人，卡西烏斯·狄奧記三千人），另有以萬計被販為奴者，阿庇安記約三萬人。與此同時，元老院承認在戰鬥中站在羅馬一方的獲自由人享有公民權，未被准許返回原莊園的義軍人員則被就地安置或流放各地。從此義大利的奴隸起義進入漫長低谷，第三次奴隸戰爭成為共和國史上規模最大、也最被記住的一次奴隸反叛，其後兩百餘年未再出現同等規模的武裝起義；它的真正遺產，是把「羅馬以軍事壓制奴隸」這個做法推到極限，同時暴露出共和國無法在奴隸制度內安置自身的困境。斯巴達克斯其人雖敗，其名卻在此後兩千年裡一直被當作不屈的象徵反覆引用。
resultEn: In 71 BC the affair ended in the breakout battle chosen by the rebels themselves. Spartacus was intercepted in Bruttium by the forces of Crassus, Philippus and Glicia and fell while forcing a way through with a few men; his body was never found, and the breakout group was wiped out to the last. The remnants were hunted down in southern Campania by the praetor Gaius Cassius Longinus, and Publius Crassus, the consul's son, fell in the fighting, so the repression lost another commander of standing. Rome closed the war with two methods, display and sale: large numbers of prisoners were nailed up along the Appian Way from Capua to Rome (Appian gives six thousand, Cassius Dio three thousand), and tens of thousands were sold into slavery, Appian giving about thirty thousand. At the same time the senate recognised the citizenship of freedmen who had fought on the Roman side, and those rebels who were not allowed back to their old estates were settled on the spot or distributed into exile. Italian slave revolts then fell into a long trough, and the Third Servile War became the largest and most remembered slave rebellion in the history of the Republic, with nothing of comparable scale following for more than two hundred years. Its real legacy was to push the method of crushing the enslaved by military force to its extreme, and at the same time to expose the Republic's inability to contain itself within the institution of slavery. Spartacus lost, but his name was carried for two thousand years afterwards as a symbol that refused to be put down.
